title: RE Leland Nichols and RE Sam Couch v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints 10-01, 13-01, and the unnumbered complaint in Case 2002-02 were all judicially out of order. Complaints 10-01 and the unnumbered complaint were filed directly with the SJC without first being filed with James River Presbytery; Complaint 13-01 challenged an action that Presbytery never took.
first_summary: The SJC ruled all three complaints in Case 2002-02 judicially out of order. Complaints 10-01 and the unnumbered complaint bypassed James River Presbytery, while Complaint 13-01 challenged a motion that had been ruled out of order and thus never became Presbytery action. The merits were not reached.
summary: Three complaints arising from Presbytery’s treatment of Session actions toward its pastor were judicially out of order. Complaints 10-01 and the unnumbered complaint were filed directly with the SJC without first being presented to James River Presbytery, contrary to BCO 43-2. Complaint 13-01 challenged an action never taken because the motion was ruled out of order. The SJC did not reach their merits. The combined decision’s pastoral-dissolution and benevolent-gift rulings concerned the other consolidated cases, not Case 2002-02.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The combined caption identifies Case 2002-02 and the parties (printed p. 72, lines 13–25); the full SJC approved the decision October 22, 2004 (printed p. 97, lines 645–655).
evidence_notes.dispute: The case arose from complaints concerning Session actions toward TE Robert Wilson and Presbytery’s treatment of those complaints (printed pp. 75–76, lines 83–95).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The judgment lists all three Case 2002-02 complaints as not judicially in order; the opinion applies BCO 43-2 to the directly filed complaints and finds no Presbytery action underlying C13-01 (printed pp. 84–86, lines 300–356).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The published concurrence expressly addresses Cases 2001-34 and 2002-03, not 2002-02; three members dissented, but no dissenting opinion is supplied (printed pp. 97–98, lines 653–671).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision supplies a material result for Case 2002-02.

source_limits: The source reports three consolidated cases and gives little description of the unnumbered Case 2002-02 complaint beyond its procedural defect. No dissenting reasoning is included.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged Presbytery handling of Session-related complaints.
score_reasons.decision: States the disposition of all three Case 2002-02 complaints.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Gives both defects: failure to file first with Presbytery and absence of an underlying action.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Shows two distinct grounds for judicial disorder without importing the consolidated merits rulings.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates Case 2002-02 from the other consolidated cases and does not treat lower-court action as the SJC disposition.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the procedural ruling.

verification_notes: Rechecked the judgment’s complete Case 2002-02 list and the separate reasoning for C10-01, C13-01, and the unnumbered complaint. The final summary was corrected to clarify that the consolidated pastoral-dissolution and gift rulings did not decide Case 2002-02.
